title: Car accessory
summary: A holder, clip or trim part inside a car. Heat, sunlight and vibration decide the material.

questions.label: Where it goes and how it attaches
questions.placeholder: e.g. clips onto the left air vent slats
questions.why: Location sets the temperature and the attachment method.

questions.label: Measured size of what it attaches to
questions.placeholder: e.g. vent slat 2.1 mm thick, 11 mm pitch
questions.why: The mating interface must be measured; it decides whether it fits at all.

questions.label: Hottest the spot gets
questions.why: A parked car in sun can exceed 80 °C at the dashboard; PLA softens near 55 °C.

questions.label: Direct sunlight
questions.why: UV weakens and discolours most filaments.

questions.label: What it carries
questions.placeholder: e.g. a 200 g phone, over bumpy roads
questions.why: Vibration and sustained load set the clip and wall sizes.

questions.label: Could it obstruct controls, view or airbags if it came loose?
questions.why: If yes, a printed part may not be acceptable at all.

material.why: PLA deforms in a hot car. ASA resists heat and UV but warps on an open printer.
material.consider: Do not promise that PLA or PETG on an open printer is adequate; test in the real spot.

checks.name: Material and process suitability
checks.why: The filament survives the hottest temperature and the sun.

checks.name: Retention under vibration
checks.why: It stays attached on rough roads; test it in the car.

checks.name: Thermal expansion
checks.why: Fits that are snug when cold may loosen or bind when hot.

checks.name: Clearance to controls
checks.why: Nothing blocks a control, the view or an airbag.

checks.name: Physical validation scope
checks.why: State which conditions a real test covered and which it did not.
